title: Finite free kernels have finite chains with quasi-coherent ideal quotients
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], I a finite index type, and p: O_X^(I) → O_X a morphism of sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. There exist a natural number n and a sequence F_j of O_X-modules such that F_0 is a zero object, F_n is isomorphic to kernel p, and for every j < n there is an ideal sheaf datum J_j on X whose associated module is quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent], and arrows a_j: F_j → F_(j+1) and b_j: F_(j+1) → J_j.toModules forming a short exact sequence. There is no vanishing-cohomology, quasi-compactness, affineness or surjectivity assumption. Terms after n are unconstrained.

source.place: Tag 01XF, label lemma-quasi-compact-h1-zero-covering, paragraph constructing F_i as the intersection with the first i direct summands; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01XF

proof.text: Induct on finite index types using Finite.induction_empty_option. For a type equivalence, apply freeFunctor.mapIso to obtain an isomorphism of free modules, precompose p with it, and transport the terminal kernel isomorphism using kernelIsIsoComp.

For PEmpty the coproduct hom-ext principle proves the identity of the free module is zero. Its kernel is zero by IsZero.of_mono applied to kernel.ι p. Choose n=0 and the constant chain kernel p; there are no quotient steps.

For Option I restrict p by freeMap some and apply the inductive hypothesis to q. The coordinate-step theorem gives a short exact kernel q → kernel p → J.toModules. If the previous chain ends at F(n) ≅ kernel q, define G(j)=F(j) for j≤n and G(j)=kernel p for j>n. Earlier quotient steps are unchanged. The last step is transported along F(n) ≅ kernel q by ShortComplex.isoMk and shortExact_of_iso. The new endpoint is kernel p itself, with its identity isomorphism. This produces n+1 steps without any cohomology or surjectivity hypothesis.

proof_origin.place: Finite.induction_empty_option implementation of the Stacks Tag 01XF coordinate filtration; empty case and isomorphism transports included.

lean.statement:
theorem finite_free_kernel_ideal_filtration (X : Scheme.{u})
    {I : Type u} [Finite I]
    (p : SheafOfModules.free (R := X.ringCatSheaf) I ⟶
      SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf) :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (F : ℕ → X.Modules),
      IsZero (F 0) ∧ Nonempty (F n ≅ kernel p) ∧
      ∀ j : ℕ, j < n → ∃ J : X.IdealSheafData,
        J.toModules.IsQuasicoherent ∧
        ∃ (a : F j ⟶ F (j + 1)) (b : F (j + 1) ⟶ J.toModules)
          (w : a ≫ b = 0), (ShortComplex.mk a b w).ShortExact
